title: Bhakti Saints Madhvacharya
definition: Madhvacharya (1238–1317 CE) was a 13th-century philosopher and the chief proponent of the Dvaita (Dualism) school of Vedanta, emphasizing the eternal distinction between the individual soul (Jiva) and the Supreme Being (Brahman/Vishnu).
importanceInUpsc: UPSC frequently tests the philosophical distinctions between Advaita (Shankara), Vishishtadvaita (Ramanuja), and Dvaita (Madhva) to assess conceptual clarity in Medieval Indian history.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Bhakti Saints Madhvacharya.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Overview of the Bhakti movement timeline
